Minister of Public Utilities and Aviation, Hon. Deodat Indar, MP, this afternoon presented and defended supplementary provisions totalling approximately G$12,938,465,377 during the Committee of Supply’s examination of Financial Paper No. 3 of 2026 at the Arthur Chung Conference Centre (ACCC), as part of the 8th Sitting of the Thirteenth Parliament.

The provisions, which were presented to the National Assembly on November 18, 2026, were examined by the Committee of Supply in accordance with constitutional requirements.

The supplementary allocations comprise G$11.33 billion for electricity services fuel comprising G$8 billion for Guyana Power and Light Inc. (GPL) and approximately G$3.33 billion to support other electricity service providers, including those serving Linden, Mabaruma, Mahdia, Port Kaituma, Moruca and Matthew’s Ridge.

G$1.56 billion for the Cheddi Jagan International Airport (CJIA) to support an expanded work programme.

G$52.44 million for hinterland electrification under the Hinterland Electrification Company Inc. (HECI).

The additional resources are in keeping with the People's Progressive Party/Civic (PPP/C)Government’s commitment to absorbing elevated fuel costs arising from global developments, ensuring that these costs are not passed on to consumers through higher electricity tariffs.

Global oil prices climbed from approximately US$71 per barrel at the end of February to a peak above US$144 per barrel in April, an increase of more than 104 per cent. By the end of October, prices remained approximately 67 per cent above pre-war levels.

The supplementary funding will support the Government’s continued investments in electricity services and aviation infrastructure while protecting households and businesses from rising electricity costs.

Guyana Power and Light Inc. (GPL) acknowledges the prolonged electricity disruption experienced by customers in sections of East Berbice from November 19, 2026.

The Company regrets the inconvenience caused and wishes to provide customers and the wider public with a detailed account of the circumstances surrounding the outage at the Canefield Substation, the technical challenges encountered, and the extensive efforts undertaken to safely restore electricity to affected communities.

The outage commenced at approximately 8:14 p.m. on Thursday, November 19, 2026, when the T2 13.8 kV incomer tripped, resulting in the loss of all circuits and a lockout of the 13.8 kV bus. 

Shortly thereafter, a flash was reported from the B4T1 cubicle following attempts to restore the system. GPL’s specialised technical team was directed to Canefield to commence investigations and restoration works.

Extensive Investigation and Testing
Upon arrival at Canefield during the early hours of Friday, November 20, the technical team commenced a systematic investigation of the substation equipment. Initial checks included controlled switching, testing of potential transformers (PTs), inspection of the busbar system, and repairs to areas where deterioration or electrical tracking was observed.

During the investigation, several equipment deficiencies were identified. These included deterioration of some PTs, condensation within the SG2 switchgear cubicle, suspect insulation and components, and poor insulation-resistance readings associated with some equipment. The team cleaned, repaired, re-insulated and tested the affected components and, where necessary, replaced suspect components.

Despite these interventions, repeated attempts to energise the system continued to result in tripping. Consequently, GPL’s technical personnel progressively isolated and tested different components in an effort to identify the source of the fault.

The ST2 auxiliary transformer was subsequently determined to be damaged based on its insulation-resistance results and was disconnected. However, another attempt to energise the bus with ST2 removed resulted in the same trip, indicating that ST2 was not the only cause of the recurring system fault.

Troubleshooting continued overnight into Saturday, November 21, with further dismantling, testing and reassembly of switchgear components. Specialist support was also engaged, resulting in further testing of the busbar, grounding transformer, switches and associated equipment.

In the course of attempting to locate the fault, the technical team undertook extensive refurbishment of the SG2 panel at the Canefield Substation, which was constructed in 1975, utilising available spare components.
A significant breakthrough was achieved at 3:30 p.m. on November 21 during another attempt to energise the system. Arcing was observed beneath metal covers over a recently installed 500 mm² cable, while the T2 transformer incomer protection relay also registered a trip. 

This development redirected the technical investigation towards the cable.
Subsequent insulation-resistance testing confirmed that the B-phase of the 500 mm² cable was defective, with a short circuit to ground. This finding provided the critical fault indication required to advance restoration efforts.

GPL’s team subsequently tested the previously installed 400 mm² incomer cable, which was found suitable for return to service. Work commenced at approximately 6:00 p.m. to reconnect the cable at the 60 MVA transformer terminal and the transformer incomer cubicle of the 13.8 kV switchgear.

Restoration of Electricity Supply
At 6:25 p.m. on Saturday, November 21, the technical team successfully re-closed the bus tie, allowing the phased restoration of electricity to affected customers to commence.

Substation operatives, working in coordination with System Control, subsequently began restoring customer feeders. Feeders F1 and F4 were energised to restore power from New Amsterdam to Mara along the eastern bank of the Berbice River, followed by F3, which serves customers between Canje and Williamsburg.
Following restoration of the main electrical system, GPL’s teams continued working to restore the substation’s auxiliary power supply.

Since the ST2 auxiliary transformer had been identified as damaged and removed from service, teams tested alternative transformers on site and installed a replacement auxiliary supply. This arrangement was completed at 1:30 a.m. on Sunday, November 22, restoring auxiliary power to the substation.

The restoration exercise required extensive diagnostic testing, as several equipment abnormalities were discovered during the investigation while repeated attempts to energise the system continued to result in protective tripping. The eventual identification of the defective B-phase of the 500 mm² cable enabled the technical team to revert to the serviceable 400 mm² cable and proceed with the restoration of customer feeders.

GPL fully recognises the significant inconvenience and disruption experienced by households, businesses and other customers in East Berbice as a result of the prolonged outage.

The Company sincerely apologises to all affected customers and thanks residents, businesses and other stakeholders for their patience and understanding while GPL’s technical teams worked continuously to identify the fault and safely restore electricity supply.

GPL also acknowledges the sustained efforts of the technical personnel involved in the troubleshooting and restoration exercise.

The Company remains committed to reviewing the circumstances surrounding the outage and the equipment deficiencies identified during the restoration process, with a view to strengthening the reliability and resilience of its infrastructure and reducing the likelihood of similar prolonged disruptions.

END

GPL CONTINUES INCREMENTAL RESTORATION OF ELECTRICITY IN EAST BERBICE FOLLOWING COMPLETION OF CANEFIELD SUBSTATION WORKS

Electricity has been successfully restored to customers along Republic Road and Strand, New Amsterdam, as well as communities stretching from Main Road, New Amsterdam to Mara.

Mr. Nandlall assured customers that GPL’s technical teams remain fully committed to restoring electricity safely to all remaining affected areas as quickly as possible. 

Mr. Nandlall emphasised that restoration is being undertaken incrementally to ensure that electricity is returned safely and reliably to each affected area. Technical teams will continue working until service has been restored to all remaining customers.

GPL also acknowledges the sustained efforts of its technical teams, who continue to work diligently to safely restore electricity to the remaining affected areas as quickly as practicable.

Customers are assured that the Company remains fully focused on completing the restoration process. Further updates will be issued as additional areas are repowered and progress continues across East Berbice.

GPL thanks its customers for their patience and cooperation as our teams work to restore electricity to every affected community.

title: PRESS RELEASE
text:
PRESS RELEASE

Guyana Power and Light Inc.
Saturday, November 21, 2026

GPL Identifies Fault at Canefield Substation; Power to Be Restored to East Berbice Communities by 1:00 PM Today

Guyana Power and Light Inc. (GPL) has identified the cause of the outage affecting customers served by the Canefield Substation in East Berbice. The problem is an insulation failure in the panel housing the substation's grounding transformer.

The grounding transformer is a key piece of safety equipment. It allows the substation's protection systems to detect faults and isolate them quickly. Because of the damage to its panel, the grounding transformer cannot be safely placed in service. Re-energising the network without it would put customers, the public and GPL personnel at risk, so the panel must be repaired before power can be restored.

Over the past two days, GPL's technical teams have worked around the clock to find the fault. GPL also brought in specialist support to help with the diagnosis. With the cause now confirmed, repairs to the panel's insulation are underway.

Barring unforeseen complications during final testing, GPL expects to complete the repairs and begin restoring power to the affected communities by 1:00 PM today. Supply may return to different areas in stages so that the network can be brought back safely.

GPL understands the hardship and frustration this prolonged outage has caused households and businesses in East Berbice. The company sincerely apologises and thanks customers for their patience.

GPL will provide further updates as the work progresses.

– END –

GPL's technical teams are currently conducting troubleshooting to identify the cause of the fault and determine the necessary corrective actions to facilitate the safe restoration of electricity supply.

Six charged with terrorism over GPL Substation fire
 Six individuals were charged today, Wednesday, November 18, 2026, with the offence of Terrorism in connection with the fire at the Guyana Power and Light (GPL) substation at Good Hope Railway Embankment, East Coast Demerara, between November 9 and 10, 2026.
 Those charged are:
 1. Alex Simpson, called “Little/Lil Man”, 30 years old, of Diamond New Scheme, East Bank Demerara.
 2. Timothy James, called “Timo”, 18 years old, of Friendship, East Coast Demerara.
 3. Yannick McCalman, called “Nick”, 33 years old, of Farm, East Bank Demerara.
 4. Osafo Browne, called “Zesser”, 20 years old, of Bladen Hall, East Coast Demerara.
 5. Shane Fordyce, 34 years old, of Herstelling, East Bank Demerara.
 6. Jonathan Cox, 29 years old, of Seventh Avenue, Diamond, East Bank Demerara.
 Timothy James was arrested on November 12, 2026, while the other five accused were arrested on November 13, 2026. All six were subsequently charged on November 18, 2026.
 They appeared before His Worship Magistrate Teriq Mohammed at the Vigilance Magistrate’s Court, where the charges were read to them. They were not required to plead.
 Timothy James was granted bail in the sum of G$99,000, while the other five accused were each granted bail in the sum of G$300,000.
 As part of their bail conditions, all six accused are required to report to the Police on the last Friday of every month and notify the Police of any change in their residential addresses. Alex Simpson, Yannick McCalman, Shane Fordyce and Jonathan Cox were also ordered to lodge their passports.
 The matter was adjourned until December 21, 2026, for report.
 Source: Guyana Police Force/Facebook/ Wednesday, November 18, 2026

 The charges stem from the alleged use of flammable substances to set fire to the GPL substation, causing damage to the facility.
 The Guyana Police Force has also indicated that further charges are pending in relation to the alleged arson attack at Strathspey School, East Coast Demerara.
 Further information is expected following their court appearance.
